source_files.role: The ported header. 208 lines: two constructors, three store overloads, nine optional-column setters, load, sixteen protected flags, eighteen protected generators and helpers - seventeen of them defined in MzTabFile.cpp and the generateMzTabSection_ template inline in the header at lines 132-143 - and fifteen protected statics that are declared and never defined.

The ported implementation, read in full. 3,352 lines: about 1,450 of reader column bookkeeping and metadata branches, about 1,300 of writer header and row generators, and the three store entry points.

The oracle. 164 lines, five START_SECTIONs, six assertion macros in total; all five sections are ported, none is merely mapped. Its generateMzTabPSMSectionRow_ section is the only place any expected cell value is written down.

Not ported here; ported by the sibling data-model package as src/format/mztab.rs. Read for the exact field list and type of every section row and of MzTabMetaData, because the reader and writer address them field by field, and for the colunit_* members, which are std::vector<std::string> while MzTabFile.cpp indexes them by a bracketed key index.
Not ported here. Read for the cell vocabulary the file layer renders and parses: which types carry the null/NaN/Inf state, which spell null as an empty payload, and the separator each list cell uses.
Shared data-model implementation, including decimal numeric modification positions and unported IDMzTabStream/CMMzTabStream exporters.
Not ported here. Read to confirm the exact toCellString of each cell type the writer calls.

Not ported here. Read for split (line 596 for the char overload, 666 for the string overload): a subject with no separator yields one field and an empty subject yields none, which is why meta_key_fields[0] is an out-of-range read for an empty MTD key cell. Also read for toInt32, whose declaration at line 49 leads to the throwing definition that makes every colunit line abort load.

Not ported. Read to reproduce the oracle's comparison: readNextLine_ at line 837 skips every empty and whitespace-only line, and the constructor at line 273 sets the *constructor* defaults to relative 1.0 and absolute 0.0 - which TEST_FILE_SIMILAR does not use, see ClassTest.cpp below. tests/mztab_file.rs::similar_lines implements the line handling, and knowing that blank lines are skipped is what revealed the doubled-blank defect its own round-trip test cannot see.

Not ported. Read to pin what TEST_FILE_SIMILAR actually compares with: TEST::isFileSimilar at lines 591-592 overrides FuzzyStringComparator's constructor defaults with absdiff_max_allowed and ratio_max_allowed, declared at lines 35 and 38 as 1E-5 and 1.+1E-5. MzTabFile_test.cpp sets no TOLERANCE_*, so the upstream store comparison runs at those tolerances, and tests/mztab_file.rs::similar_line - which requires exact f64 equality - is stricter than upstream rather than equal to it.

fixtures.role: Unmodified upstream. 1,291 lines, the largest reference document: Complete/Quantification, 199 MTD lines covering every metadata key family, 6 ms_runs, 12 assays, 2 study variables, and PRT (57 rows), PEP (80) and PSM (946) sections. Four optional columns in the protein section and two in the peptide section, and a peptide optional cell whose text is NaN, which is a string and not the numeric NaN state. Its PRH declares no num_peptides_distinct/unique columns at all, which is what exercises an absent column family. Two COM lines and four blank lines, two of them adjacent around a comment, which is the case that distinguishes this port's blank restoration from the source's.

Unmodified upstream. 97 lines with six COM lines interleaved inside the metadata and both data sections, and two blank lines; the test that asserts comments and blanks stay on their original line numbers uses this file. 3 ms_runs, PRT and PSM only, and a PSH header line with a trailing space that TextFile's line trimming removes.
Unmodified upstream. 104 lines. Its PRH declares all three num_* families over all six runs, and its PRT rows carry negative and null score values in the ms-run score columns.
Unmodified upstream. 115 lines, the widest header: 16 assays and 4 study variables, so 16 + 12 quantification columns in the protein section.

Unmodified upstream. The only reference document with an SML section, the only one with CRLF line endings, and the only one whose mzTab-version is not a dotted triple ('1.0 rc5'). Summary/Identification, no assays and no study variables, a five-element sample_processing parameter list, two instrument analyzers, two software entries with a setting, and parameter cells with empty cv_label and accession such as '[ , , CHEMMOD:2M+H, ]'.

Added by this package; not upstream. Non-ASCII throughout: a Japanese COM line, mzTab-ID and description, an em dash and a Greek capital omega in the description, a URL with Japanese path segments, and an opt_global_ column whose name and value are Japanese. Its second PSM row's sequence is a run of two-byte characters. It also carries a colunit-psm key, which no upstream fixture has because the C++ reader throws on one, and the three numeric states: a NaN calc_mass_to_charge, an Inf score and a null calc_mass_to_charge. Every numeric value has an exact binary representation and the metadata is already in the writer's order, so the round trip is asserted byte for byte.

source_anchors.operation: extractBracketIndex: substitute the prefix away, remove every ']', trim, StringUtils::toInt32. Returns a signed Int that every caller casts to Size, so assay[0] yields key 0 and assay[-1] yields SIZE_MAX
the constructor lists all sixteen optional-column flags and sets every one to false
extractIndexPairsFromBrackets_ leaves either member of the pair at 0 when its regex does not match, producing the column family member '...[0]' that the format does not define
the read loop increments line_number in the for-statement, so a continue still advances it: comment and empty-row positions are indices into the whole file
a line whose trimmed length is under three bytes is recorded as an empty row and never dispatched to a section
a data line with fewer than three tab-separated cells throws Exception::ParseError
the MTD key is split on '-' and meta_key_fields[0] is read unconditionally; StringUtils::split clears the vector for an empty subject, so an empty key cell makes this an out-of-range read
the first of thirty-two MTD branches that index meta_key_fields[1] without checking the field count; 'MTD instrument[1] value' reads past the end of the vector
two further MTD branches index meta_key_fields[2] without checking the field count
the colunit-protein branch calls extractBracketIndex(meta_key_fields[0], "colunit[") on the literal key 'colunit', so StringUtils::toInt32 throws a ConversionError: every MTD colunit line aborts load
PRH optional columns are discovered by the 'opt_' prefix and keyed by name in a std::map, so row.opt_ is filled in lexicographic order whatever order the header used
the twenty mandatory-column checks begin; each writes to std::cout once per data row and never reaches the caller
PRT row cells are read as cells[index] with no bounds check, and index 0 means 'the header omitted this column', which is also the index of the section tag
the PEH 'uri' column index is assigned to protein_uri_index: the peptide uri is never read, and a later PRT row reads its protein uri from the peptide section's column number
the PEP branch inserts "PRT" into sections_present instead of "PEP"
the peptide uri assignment is commented out with the note 'always false'
the PSH 'uri' column index is likewise assigned to protein_uri_index
PSH optional columns are matched with cells[i] == "opt_" for exact equality rather than by prefix, so every optional column of a PSM section is dropped on load
the read loop ends: load handles MTD, COM, PRH/PRT, PEH/PEP, PSH/PSM and SMH/SML only. NUH/NUC, OLH/OLI and OSH/OSM are never parsed, although store writes all three
hasMandatoryMetaDataKeys_ is commented out, which is why sections_present has no consumer
generateMzTabMetaDataSection_ writes mzTab-version, mzTab-mode and mzTab-type unconditionally, then title and mzTab-ID only when set, then description unconditionally
nucleic_acid_search_engine_score, oligonucleotide_search_engine_score and osm_search_engine_score are written; none of the three is ever read back
a software[n] line is written even when the term is null, unlike every other optional metadata key

colunit-protein is written as the key concatenated with the value and no separator at all, so the reader sees a two-cell line; and the PSM key is written 'colunit-PSM' while the reader matches the lower-case 'psm'
the protein header emits the search_engine_score[s]_ms_run[r] columns runs-outer, scores-inner

the protein row emits the same values scores-outer, runs-inner: the counts agree so the postcondition stays silent, and with two or more scores and two or more runs the values land under the wrong headers
the protein row's quantification cells are looked up by the metadata's assay and study_variable keys, with MzTabString().toCellString() as the fallback, which is the null cell
the peptide header repeats the runs-outer, scores-inner order

the peptide row advances the study-variable value, stdev and std_error iterators in lock-step and stops at the first exhausted one, so a row with no standard deviations writes no study-variable columns at all

the PSM row writes a single literal 'null' score cell when the row's score map is empty, a workaround for identifications without hits that matches the header only when it declared exactly one score column
the small-molecule header declares one smallmolecule_abundance_assay[n] column per assay

the small-molecule row jumps from modifications straight to the study-variable triple and never emits the assay cells the header declared, so any document with an assay fails the column-count postcondition and cannot be written

the nucleic-acid header numbers num_osms_ms_run, num_oligos_distinct_ms_run and num_oligos_unique_ms_run from zero, alone among all bracketed families, while the row writer emits the values keyed from one
addOptionalColumnsToSectionRow_ searches the row's entries linearly per requested name, breaks on the first match, and writes MzTabString("null") for a miss, which is the null cell
store(filename, MzTab) rejects an extension that is neither mzTab nor tsv with Exception::UnableToCreateFile, then opens the destination with ios::trunc before anything is validated
in Complete mode the peptide section declares a score column for every ms_run of the metadata whether or not a row carries one; otherwise only when at least one row has run-level scores
the PSM score column count is capped at one with the comment that only the main score is stored, a limit of the exporters rather than of the format
generateMzTabNucleicAcidHeader_ is called with its second and third arguments transposed relative to its signature (search_ms_runs, n_best_search_engine_scores, n_search_engine_scores)

the comment and blank restoration inserts a blank whenever the current position was blank in the original file, even though the generated lines already carry one before each section, so every separator is emitted twice; and the loop stops as soon as the generated lines run out, dropping any comment or blank recorded past that point, which this port instead walks on to emit (positions shift up by the width of any gap, since nothing fills it)
generateMzTabSection_ throws Exception::Postcondition when a header and a row disagree on the column count: 'Header and content differs in columns. Please report this bug to the OpenMS developers.'
the first of fifteen protected static members declared here and defined nowhere in the tree; the run ends at line 201 with writeProteinData_
friend class MzTabMFile, which is why the generators are protected rather than private
Modification positions use the decimal numeric append overloads declared by StringUtils.h; the earlier character-narrowing claim is withdrawn.
readNextLine_ skips every empty and whitespace-only line, which is why the upstream round-trip test cannot see the doubled blank lines

TEST::isFileSimilar overrides FuzzyStringComparator's constructor defaults with absdiff_max_allowed and ratio_max_allowed, which are 1E-5 and 1.+1E-5 at ClassTest.cpp:35 and 38 unless a test sets TOLERANCE_*; MzTabFile_test.cpp sets neither, so TEST_FILE_SIMILAR tolerates 1e-5 absolute / 1+1e-5 relative there, while tests/mztab_file.rs::similar_line requires exact f64 equality and is therefore stricter

evidence: Tier 3, source review, with a tier 3 round trip over the retained upstream reference documents. MzTabFile_test.cpp has five START_SECTIONs and six assertion macros in total; all five sections are ported rather than mapped, and the four transcribed cell literals ('null', 'NDYKAPPQPAPGK', '0.0420992', 'null', the last four cells of a PSM row) are the only expected output values the upstream suite writes down anywhere. Transcribed C++ literals are tier 3 evidence. The five reference documents are the other half: each is loaded, written and compared with the original through tests/mztab_file.rs::similar_lines, which reproduces the upstream comparison except that it is stricter on numbers (sort the lines, remove every space, skip the blank ones as FuzzyStringComparator::readNextLine_ does, and compare numbers numerically; upstream's TEST_FILE_SIMILAR tolerates 1e-5 absolute / 1+1e-5 relative through TEST::isFileSimilar, this requires exact f64 equality). Each is also written to disk, read back and compared as a model, which is stronger than any text comparison because it covers the null/NaN/Inf state of every numeric cell, the optional columns of every row, and the recorded comment and blank-line positions. The additional unicode fixture round-trips byte for byte. Everything else - the four resource ceilings, the hostile headers and metadata keys, the non-ASCII output paths, the error-variant choices, and every test of a divergence listed in docs/MZTAB_FILE_SUPPORT.md - is independently derived (tier 4). No full format implementation was built or executed and no format output was retained, so this is not a tier 1 differential: the reference .mzTab files are upstream *inputs* that its own suite round-trips, not outputs a C++ build produced here.
gaps: store(filename, protein_identifications, peptide_identifications, ...) is not ported: it builds rows through MzTab::IDMzTabStream, which is not in the crate.
store(filename, ConsensusMap, ...) is not ported: it builds rows through MzTab::CMMzTabStream, which is not in the crate.
The MapAccPepType typedef and the fifteen protected statics of MzTabFile.h:151-201 are not ported; all fifteen are declared and defined nowhere in the pinned tree.
friend class MzTabMFile has no Rust equivalent. MzTabMFile is implemented in mztab_m; the proteomics generators remain public native methods.
sections_present is not ported: the source fills it but its only consumer, hasMandatoryMetaDataKeys_, is commented out at MzTabFile.cpp:1547.

No tier 1 differential exists for this header. Reaching one needs an oracle driver that links the prebuilt C++ and prints a stored document, because the upstream suite retains no MzTabFile output - only its inputs.

The reliability, uri and go_terms columns are optional in the format, so a document written with one of the sixteen flags cleared does not round-trip a row carrying that cell. MzTabFile::lossless sets all sixteen.

A section header declares one column set for every row, so an indexed family member that only some rows carry becomes a null cell, and therefore a null entry, in the rest. The file cannot express 'absent' as distinct from 'null'.
The port is serial, as the source is: MzTabFile.cpp carries no OpenMP directive, so there is no parallelism gap to record.

An indexed metadata group survives a round trip only if at least one of its keys has a non-null value, because every optional metadata key is skipped when null. A document whose assay[1] is declared only by 'MTD assay[1]-sample_ref null' loses the key and the abundance column the layout would have declared. Shared with the source; closing it needs a record of declared-versus-valued keys that neither the source nor MzTabMetaData has. No reference document is affected.

CI wiring, the docs/core-sdk-reviewed-apis.json ledger entry, the docs/VALIDATION.md checkpoint, the README.md row and the CHANGELOG.md line are outside this package's writable set and are handed to the integrating agent.
numeric_operator_review: The earlier claimed character narrowing was withdrawn after checking pinned StringUtils.h and an isolated executed overload-resolution probe. No full mzTab/MSDataWritingConsumer or full SDK C++ execution is claimed.
external_reference_note: Isolated overload-resolution probe, compiled and run on kim with GCC13.3 C++20. Numeric global overload block copied from pinned StringUtils.h; appendToStr functions replaced by std::to_string adapters and Size by std::size_t. No full SDK include closure or linking; proves presence/selectability of numeric overloads in OpenMS namespace contexts and falsifies the claim only char overloads exist.
